claims.text: The alloy has the composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The as-cast alloy solidifies with several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
The alloy follows a complex, multistep crystallization sequence during cooling and reheating.
Alternating rapid-quench and mild-reheating pulses will significantly increase amorphous-phase retention.
The pulse-cooling cycle will enhance thermal stability.
Pulse cooling disrupts early nucleation events responsible for extensive primary crystallization.
The rapid-quench portions of the cycle operate at approximately 10^3 K/s.
The reheating pulses are maintained between Tg and 0.8 times Tx.
Keeping reheating pulses within the specified temperature interval prevents full crystallite growth.
Mild reheating temporarily increases local atomic mobility.
The increased mobility relieves concentration fluctuations.
The increased mobility dissipates residual stresses accumulated during rapid quenching.
Stress and concentration-fluctuation relief resets early nucleation events.
Resetting early nucleation events inhibits growth of the primary crystalline phases.
Pulse-cooled specimens will have a higher retained amorphous fraction than continuously quenched controls.
Pulse-cooled specimens will exhibit diminished crystallization exotherms during DSC reheating.
Pulse-cooled specimens will exhibit delayed crystallization exotherms during DSC reheating.
Pulse cooling will shift the crystallization onset temperature upward.
Continuous rapid cooling followed by conventional reheating typically produces significant primary crystallization and lower amorphous retention in this alloy.

contradictions.description: The treatment is said to consist of alternating quench and reheating cycles applied continuously from the liquid state to room temperature, but every reheating pulse is also required to remain within the much narrower Tg-to-0.8·Tx interval. The protocol does not explain how both requirements can hold outside that interval.
